bugs.title: Re-asked question can never be re-confirmed: same-value enter is an inert no-op that leaves the question stuck in `reasked` forever
bugs.description: The re-ask loop dead-ends when the user's answer has not changed. Per the spec's auto-close algorithm (state-and-persistence.md §Auto-close: 'on tool_execution_end (interrogate, action=upsert): mark each touched submitted question reasked'), ANY upsert touching a submitted id flips it to `reasked` while KEEPING its answer (rule-1 same-options re-asks). The state machine requires 'reasked → user answers → answered(pending)', but acceptOptionIndex's ANSWER-PIN-001 same-value no-op (src/panel/actions.ts:294) checks only answer PRESENCE, with no status exclusion: pressing enter (or a digit) on the still-recorded value does NOT re-answer the question. The question stays `reasked` indefinitely: it counts as unanswered everywhere (nextUnanswered/completeness/widget), so AUTOSUBMIT-001 can never fire (no commit ever happens), ctrl+s reports 'nothing to submit' (reasked ids are not in the pending set and produce no diff), and the agent_settled close pass only closes `submitted`. Completion (FR-5, the full-record injection that is the product's deliverable) is permanently blocked unless the user changes their answer to a DIFFERENT value or a write-in — directly contradicting commitment 8 ('Always keep the user's answer. No exceptions.') and FR-3/FR-21/AC-3's re-ask round-trip. ANSWER-PIN-001's no-op ruling was authored to stop re-PROPOSAL of settled answers on revisit; applying it verbatim to the hybrid reasked+kept-answer state (created by the lifecycle marker, not by the user) breaks the re-ask confirmation loop.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Upsert one choice question (options a/b), panel: accept 'a' (cursor 0), ctrl+s → status submitted, submission delivered, epoch 2. 2. Agent re-asks with the SAME option values (rule-1 text edit, correct rev+epoch) and the host fires tool_execution_start/end for the upsert → lifecycle marks q1 `reasked` with answer 'a' KEPT. 3. User reopens the panel: caret is pinned to the recorded 'a' row (initialCursorIndex). Press enter → acceptOptionIndex returns "noop": status remains `reasked`, no state write. 4. Press ctrl+s → submit() early-returns with flash 'nothing to submit'; no message, no epoch bump. 5. No user gesture except changing the answer value (different option, or a write-in) can clear `reasked`; until then completion can never fire. Verified end-to-end via vite-node probe driving only public seams (executeInterrogate + lifecycle event bus + InterrogationPanel + accept/submit): after the re-ask, 'after enter on recorded value: reasked', 'after ctrl+s: flash: nothing to submit', deliveries unchanged.

bugs.title: Re-answering a rule-2 re-ask with the same value records the answer but ships nothing: 'nothing to submit' despite a pending answer, forever undeliverable
bugs.description: When the agent re-asks with CHANGED options (merge rule 2: answer deleted, status reasked) and the user re-selects the SAME value (still present among the new options), applyAnswer records the answer and flips status to `answered` (pending) — but the last submission's snapshot already holds that identical value, and computeDiff is answer-signature-only (status-blind). submit()'s early return `if (diff.changed.length === 0 || userChanged.length === 0)` (src/panel/actions.ts:595) then fires on EVERY attempt: no delivery, no epoch bump, footer flash 'nothing to submit' even though a pending (answered) answer exists. maybeAutoSubmit's transition firing is equally dead — it calls the same submit() pipeline which early-returns, so the AUTOSUBMIT-001 contract ('the identical submission pipeline fires automatically' when the commit answers the last unanswered question) is violated with zero feedback (shipped=false means not even the 'submitted — n answer(s)' flash). The agent never receives a submission message; the close pass only archives `submitted`; completion (FR-5) is blocked. This is exactly the bug class the decision ledger says was found and fixed for the (since removed) remote-bridge path — D-R6: 'bridge submissions flush answered→submitted even when the diff is empty (identical re-selections after a rule-1 re-ask)… found by the live RPC itest as completion deadlocks' — but the panel path retained the zero-diff early return. Violates FR-3 ('ctrl+s submits all pending answers immediately'), AUTOSUBMIT-001/003, AC-2/AC-2c.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Upsert q1 with options [a,b,c]; panel: accept 'a', ctrl+s → submitted, snapshot S1 (answer=a), epoch 2. 2. Agent rule-2 re-ask (options changed to [a,b,d], correct rev+epoch) → answer deleted, status reasked. 3. User re-accepts 'a' → status `answered`, answer=a. 4. Auto-submit on the completeness transition ships NOTHING (submit early-returns: diff vs S1 is empty). 5. ctrl+s → flash 'nothing to submit'; deliveries count unchanged; epoch unchanged; q1 stuck `answered`-pending — invisible to the model until the user picks a different value. Verified end-to-end via vite-node probe: 'after re-answer: answered a', 'auto-submit deliveries: 1' (only the round-1 submission), 'after ctrl+s: flash: nothing to submit'.

bugs.title: FR-18 invalidation confirm bypassed when editing a CLOSED (archived) question — answered dependents are silently invalidated
bugs.description: The FR-18 ripple-confirm seam fires only when the EDITED question's status is `answered` or `submitted` (src/panel/actions.ts:302 in acceptOptionIndex; :392 in writeInEnter; src/panel/panel.ts:863 in stageText). Editing an archived (closed) question is fully supported (FR-2: 'including archived ones… Editing re-marks a question pending'; AC-13), and a closed question still carries its recorded answer — but its edits skip the seam entirely and apply directly, then run evaluateDependsOn, which silently moots the invalidated answered/submitted dependents. The user-specified Q39=B UX ('give them an overview of how many previously-answered questions they're invalidating… force them to accept or cancel' — a defaulted decision the user explicitly worded) and state-and-persistence.md's unconditional 'Answer edits apply through the ripple confirm before entering answered(pending)' are both violated for a whole class of edits: real user answers are destroyed (mooted) with no confirmation. Verified by probe: db=closed + scale=answered(dependsOn db=postgres): changing db to sqlite applies with confirmMode NONE and flips scale answered→moot silently, while the identical edit on an answered (non-closed) db correctly raises the keep/cancel modal.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Seed: q1 'db' (options sqlite/postgres) answered+submitted then closed by the close pass; q2 'scale' answered (pending) with dependsOn [{id:'db', equals:'postgres'}]. 2. Open the panel, navigate to q1 (R1: closed questions navigable; caret pins to the recorded 'postgres' row — FR-35 works). 3. Move the cursor to 'sqlite' (a DIFFERENT choice) and press enter. Expected: FR-18 modal '⚠ Invalidates 1 answered questions… enter=keep, esc=cancel'. Actual: no modal; q1 → answered sqlite; q2 answered→moot instantly, silently (probe output: 'confirmMode after accept on CLOSED db: NONE — silent apply', 'scale: moot'). Same bypass on the write-in commit path (actions.ts:392) and the elaboration-save path (panel.ts:863).

bugs.title: FR-17 moot reason never rendered in the panel: short view and overview show a generic or actively misleading substitute instead of 'moot: {dep}={value}'
bugs.description: FR-17 requires unmet questions to 'grey out as moot with reason (`moot: storage=sqlite`)' — the h2.29-format reason naming the dependency and its value, which depends-on.ts computes (dependencyMet/failReason → evaluateDependsOn().mootered). No panel view ever renders it: the only consumer of the computed reason is delivery.ts:420 (the completion record). The short view derives its reason from the MOOT QUESTION'S OWN answer value or falls back to 'dependency changed' (src/panel/short-view.ts:149 mootReason), and the overview prefers the question's own elaboration text then its own value (src/panel/overview.ts:167 overviewMootReason) — so a user looking at a mooted question sees '⊘ moot — dependency changed' (which dependency? which value?) or, worse, the moot question's own now-invalid answer presented as the cause. The UI tests are masked by fixtures that pre-bake the literal string 'moot: storage=sqlite' into the fixture's answer.text (overview.test.ts:205-279), which never happens on the production path. Violates FR-17's explicit reason format, AC-6 ('dependent greys as moot with reason'), and ui-spec's overview contract '⊘ moot (+reason, dimmed)'; the audit-trail quality (Q34=A) degrades to a non-explanation in the interactive views even though the correct reason is available at render time.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Upsert q1 'storage' (options sqlite/postgres, gate group) and q2 with dependsOn [{id:'storage', equals:'postgres'}]. 2. Answer q1=sqlite → evaluateDependsOn mootered q2 with reason 'moot: storage=sqlite' (verified in the evaluator's return value). 3. Render the short view for q2 (renderShortViewOptions): line reads '⊘ moot — dependency changed' — the computed reason is discarded. 4. With q2 carrying its own (now-invalid) answer 'big', the short view renders '⊘ moot — big' (the question's own answer shown as the moot cause) and layout.ts statusMarkers renders just '⊘ moot'. 5. buildOverviewContent/overviewMootReason likewise never consult dependencyMet; only buildCompletion (delivery.ts:420) shows the true 'moot: storage=sqlite'.

bugs.title: First upsert of a new interrogation after completion always rejects an honest epoch echo with a spurious STALE
bugs.description: After an interrogation completes (state.completed=true, epoch retained), a model that follows the tool's own guidance ('include the epoch from your last read/result') echoes the last-reported epoch on the first upsert of the NEW interrogation. executeInterrogate swaps in a fresh receiver state (epoch 1, per the 2026-09-14 BUG-002 pin) and then runs assertFresh against THAT state (src/tool.ts:300), so any honest echo (epoch ≥ 2) mismatches epoch 1 and throws 'STALE: session epoch is 1 (you sent 2). Changes since epoch 2: (none). Re-apply against current state.' Every conforming model pays one wasted error round-trip per new interrogation before self-healing (dropping the epoch or sending 1). The spec's guard contract does promise one-round-trip self-healing, so this is friction rather than a hard failure — but the completed-swap path makes the staleness signal meaningless (nothing actually changed since the sent epoch: the digest is '(none)'), and the 2026-09-14 pin explicitly intended first-upserts to be guard-friendly.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Upsert q1, answer, submit, settle, complete → completed=true, epoch 2 (read returns 'epoch 2'). 2. Model sends {goal:'g2', epoch:2, questions:[{id:'n1',…}]} (new ids only, echoing the epoch the tool last reported). 3. executeInterrogate swaps to fresh state (epoch 1) and assertFresh's epoch guard throws the STALE error ('Changes since epoch 2: (none)'). 4. Retrying without the epoch (or with 1) succeeds — one spurious rejection per new interrogation for epoch-echoing models.

summary: End-to-end PRD validation of pi-interrogator. Baseline: the full suite (46 files, 1265 tests) and typecheck are green. I then probed the implementation adversarially with headless vite-node scripts over the public seams (executeInterrogate, lifecycle event bus, InterrogationPanel + actions/renderers, merge/guards/caps, delivery, fallback, discuss, duty derivation): answer pinning (FR-35/AC-16) works exactly as spec'd across all statuses and entry paths (pin, digit/deep/write-in no-ops, buffer consumption, editor-close re-seed, D-R13 display mapping); auto-submit rules (a/b) and gate hold behave per AUTOSUBMIT-001/002/003; surfacing gates (SURFACE-001/002), merge rules, rev/epoch guards, caps/min-floors, write-in/elaboration duties, delta shaping, completion record, schema validation (duplicate ids, choice-without-options, bad recommendation) and dependency-cycle safety all check out. The five reported bugs cluster in two underspecified seams: (1) the re-ask/re-confirmation loop — an agent re-ask followed by the user confirming their unchanged answer wedges the interrogation in both re-ask flavors (same-value enter swallowed leaving permanent `reasked`; same-value re-answer recorded but undeliverable with a lying 'nothing to submit'), blocking the completion injection that is the product's core deliverable — a bug class the decision ledger shows was known and fixed on the since-removed bridge path but survives in the panel pipeline; and (2) status-gated spec clauses applied too literally (FR-18's modal skipped for closed edits; FR-17's dependency reason computed but never rendered). Overall quality is high — the codebase is unusually rigorous — which makes the silent re-ask wedges the standout release blockers.
recommendations: In submit(), treat pending (answered) ids as user shipments even when the answer-signature diff is empty — flush them to submitted and deliver (the D-R6 bridge fix pattern: 'flush answered→submitted even when the diff is empty'), or include question status in the diff signature so a re-ask reset + same-value re-answer is visible.

Exclude `reasked` from the ANSWER-PIN-001 same-value no-op in acceptOptionIndex/writeInEnter (or have the no-op re-mark the question answered) so a rule-1 re-ask can be confirmed without changing the answer's value.
Extend the FR-18 ripple-seam status gate (acceptOptionIndex:302, writeInEnter:392, stageText in panel.ts:863) to fire for ANY edited question carrying a recorded answer, including `closed`.

Render the real dependency-derived moot reason in the panel: either persist evaluateDependsOn's h2.29 reason on the question or call dependencyMet at render time in short-view.ts/overview.ts/layout.ts, and replace the fixture-baked 'moot: storage=sqlite' strings in the tests with production-path scenarios.

Exempt the completed-swap fresh-state path from the epoch equality check (accept any epoch on the first upsert against a freshly swapped state) so honest epoch echoes stop paying a spurious STALE round trip.
